name: Kreislauf
prior: NoInputMixer (Igor Vasiliev, iOS/macOS 2023, standalone + AUv3): seven-channel mixer with an eight-slot FX rack, 'an experimental feedback instrument' modelling an analog console, MIDI learn (VS: synthtopia.com 2023/09/14, sonicstate.com 2023/09/13) = feedback as an instrument on a phone, mixer metaphor, no pitch field. Rhizomatic Plasmonic (Clevinger 2020, VST3/AU/standalone): 'a self-oscillating delay-based waveguide / multimode ladder filter pair', impulse/noise/wavetable exciters feeding the loop, delays that also self-oscillate, 'sounds unreachable in other synths', CPU heavy (VS: kvraudio.com/product/plasmonic-by-rhizomatic, synthanatomy.com p=51085, rekkerd.org p=167362; R: musicians.md 2.6) = closest mechanism, desktop. Barrel Synth (CCRMA 2022, browser): no-input-mixer-style feedback matrix between chaotic comb voices (VS: ccrma.stanford.edu/~jomitch/220a/fp). Nicolas Collins, Pea Soup (1974): 'self-stabilizing feedback network' tuned to the room, software emulation downloadable (VS: nicolascollins.com/texts/PeaSoup2020.pdf, cdm.link). Hardware: Halldorophone (string feedback, Bela in the loop; VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halldorophone, nime.org/proc/nime2023_51), Finegear Modmix (each channel 'routed back into itself to act as a sound generator'; VS: schneidersladen.de), NIMB-O no-input pedal (VS: rockboard.de), 2HP Comb (comb 'driven into self oscillation' with a damping filter in the loop; VS: dupertuis.com), Steampipe (Reaktor/Elektron feedback-delay instrument with 'complex tuning compensation' for loop filters; VS: elektronauts.com/t/octatrack-steampipe). Textbook: 'a very short delay becomes a comb filter, which becomes a pitch... feedback sustains it' (VS: beatkitchen.io; Max MSP delay tutorial 6, docs.cycling74.com). Research model identical to the idea (R: synthesis.md 2.14: delay + bandpass + saturation + gain, 'Larsen-Atmen'; 'Larsen-Quelle als Instrument' listed as unoccupied). Not found: a pitch-field voice whose loop gain sits under the finger with the tipping point mid-travel and attack = time-to-tone.
costNotes: Per voice ~13 native nodes (sum, bandpass, shaper, gain, delay, HP, raum delay + gain, LP, noise + click sources, detune gain + shaper) x 0.03 = 0.4-0.45 units (R: webaudio.md section 4) - the idea's 0.45 holds. L3 two loops ~0.9 only without oversampling: a 2x WaveShaper costs ~8-10 biquads (~0.25-0.3 units) each (R: section 7) and, worse, adds its 128-tap kernel latency (~1.3 ms at 48 kHz, browser-specific, not exposed to JS) inside the loop - at tau 4.5 ms that is a -25 % pitch error - so never oversample inside the cycle (a 2x shaper after the loop is fine). Cycle rule: delayTime is clamped to >= one render quantum in a cycle (V: spec_index.bs 7768-7770; wpt_feedback_delay.html) and is otherwise a normal fractional delay (A: the spec only clamps the minimum; the 'multiples of 128 frames' remark in webaudio.md section 7 is not in the spec text - verify on device with the bench), so tau = n/f with n = ceil(128 f/SR) works: n = 1 to 375 Hz, 2 to 750 Hz, 5 at 1760 Hz. Mode spacing f/n: at n = 5 the neighbours sit +-20 % (+-3 HT) away and a Q = 14 bandpass attenuates them ~14 dB (A) - enough to lock, hops possible under fast gain changes (raise Q with n, as the idea says). Pitch: the biquad has zero phase at its centre, linear-interpolated delay error < 1 ct up to 2 kHz (A). Bebung: a Gain(-tau ln2/1200) from the cent bus into delayTime (linear, < 0.2 % error at +-100 ct) is simpler than a per-note WaveShaper curve; bq.detune takes v.mod directly (APP 3464). Voice end must break the cycle (g -> 0 then disconnect) or the loop keeps rendering after finish().
soundHeld: Below the tipping point (y < 0.45, g 0.99-1.0) the voice is a noise-knocked comb that rings and decays - Saite/Karplus territory with a long 'Oliveros' tail near g = 0.995 (decay ~0.9 s per e-fold at tau 4.5 ms, A); above it the tone swells in (~0.3-0.5 s at anschwellen 1.12 with n = 2) and locks into a tanh-limited near-sine: the steady state is a whistle with a little odd-harmonic colour and the raum comb's ripple, close to Tiefe/Hauch in timbre. The distinctiveness is the behaviour - patience, swell, lock, the finger as microphone distance, chords as a Larsen choir with independent swell times - a true regime switch under Hoehe (R: musicians.md P1), not the sound. Two real defects: per-pass growth makes the swell time proportional to tau, so a 110-Hz note (tau 9.1 ms) swells half as fast as a 440-Hz note (define growth per second: g = anschwellen^(tau / 4.5 ms)); and just above the tipping point the level creeps up for seconds and then clips into tanh, a +20 dB swell on one held finger - the RMS cap must act on g (AGC), not on the output.
soundBurst: Puls: a hard knock + g = anschwellen for the gate, then 0.96: at 440 Hz a 160-ms gate is 35 loop passes = +34 dB, the click becomes a squeal within the gate ('Quietscher') and decays over ~0.8 s; at 110 Hz the same gate is 17 passes = +17 dB, a pluck with a slight swell, no squeal; at 1/16 120 bpm (112 ms, APP 5980) only high lanes squeal. With per-second growth it becomes consistent: knock -> rising squeal -> decaying howl, a hit no other engine has. 0.8-s tails on 1/16 patterns pile up - the release must scale with the step (gate = 0.9 x step is passed in).
failureModes: Oversampled WaveShaper inside the cycle adds unreported kernel latency -> up to -25 % pitch error, different per browser; keep oversample 'none' in the loop
Swell time and Puls squeal depend on tau (per-pass gain): low notes never reach the howl inside a gate - define growth per second
Locked steady state is a near-sine whistle (Tiefe/Hauch territory); needs raum ripple, biss and a Hoehe-coupled colour or it bores after the swell
Level creep: just above the tipping point the loop climbs into tanh over seconds; AGC on g, plus a master cap for a four-finger Larsen choir
Mode hops at high n (f/5 neighbours 3 HT away) when gain changes fast; Q must rise with n, and k-rate detune steps (Firefox) can kick the loop
Release = gain ramp, not an envelope: finger up still howls for ~0.8 s; stealing mid-howl needs vFade, and Puls tails must shorten with the step
In-cycle delay semantics on device unverified (A): bench a 2-period loop at 440 Hz for pitch accuracy before building
verdict: Rare in mechanism, common in sound: the loop (delay + bandpass + saturation + gain > 1) is the textbook self-oscillating comb that Plasmonic (2020) makes its heart, NoInputMixer (iOS/mac 2023) sells as a mixer, Barrel Synth runs in a browser and Steampipe/2HP Comb do in hardware; the finger-held loop gain with a tipping point mid-travel in a pitch field is unfound. Native-feasible at ~0.45 units (L3 ~0.9) thanks to the n-period delay trick, but never oversample inside the cycle (kernel latency detunes the loop by up to 25 %) and growth must be defined per second, not per loop pass, or swell times and Puls squeals differ by octave. Musically the behaviour (patience, swell, lock, Larsen choir) is distinctive while the locked steady state is a near-sine whistle; it earns its place if the RMS cap acts on the gain, Q rises with n, and the knock/squeal Puls hit is tuned to the step length.
